t:
That the first sect ion of the Act of August 4, 1950 (64 Stat. 411; 2 U.S.C. 167) is amended to read as follows:


“(a) 
The Librarian of Congress may designate employees of the Library of Congress as special policemen for duty in connection with the policing of the Library of Congress buildings and grounds and adjacent streets and shall fix their rates of basic pay as follows:

“(1) 
Private—not to exceed the rate for GS–5, Step 5;


“(2) 
Sergeant—not to exceed the rate for GS–6, Step 5;


“(3) 
Lieutenant—not to exceed the rate for GS–7. Step 5;


“(4) 
Senior Lieutenant—not to exceed the rate for GS–9, Step 5; and


“(5) 
Captain—not to exceed the rate for GS–10, Step 5.



“(b) 
The Librarian of Congress may apply the provisions of subchapter V of chapter 55 of title 5, United States Code, to members of special police force of the Library of Congress.”

fable.w: The tempting reading is that designating people as special policemen brings individuals into a government process, but those designated are Library of Congress employees, who are inside the federal government. The section only authorizes the Librarian to designate special police and fix their pay rates. It involves no consultation with outside parties, no public comment or hearing, no advisory body with non-federal members, no rulemaking, and no right to sue.
fable.s: The Librarian of Congress may designate employees of the Library of Congress as special policemen

qwen_block.w: This section authorizes the Librarian of Congress to designate federal employees as special policemen and sets their pay rates. All actors involved (the Librarian, Library of Congress employees) are inside the federal government. There is no consultation, coordination, or participation with any outside party such as the public, states, or private entities.
qwen_block.s: The Librarian of Congress may designate employees of the Library of Congress as special policemen for duty in connection with the policing of the Library of Congress buildings and grounds and adjacent streets and shall fix their rates of basic pay as follows:

opus.w: The section lets the Librarian of Congress name Library employees as special police, set their pay, and apply federal pay rules to them. Everyone involved works for the federal government, and no one outside it is consulted or given a role. Mentions of 'policing' or official designations might look procedural, but the decision never involves an outside party.
opus.s: The Librarian of Congress may designate employees of the Library of Congress as special policemen

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes the Librarian of Congress to designate federal employees (employees of the Library of Congress) as special policemen and sets their pay rates. All actors involved (the Librarian, the employees) are inside the federal government. There is no consultation, coordination, or participation with any outside party such as the public, states, or private entities.
qwen_chat.s: The Librarian of Congress may designate employees of the Library of Congress as special policemen for duty in connection with the policing of the Library of Congress buildings and grounds and adjacent streets and shall fix their rates of basic pay as follows:
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "special policemen" are outside parties or that the Librarian is consulting with them. However, the text explicitly states these are "employees of the Library of Congress," which are federal employees. Therefore, any interaction is internal to the federal government.
